atlas.name: Zeús
steps: The Greek form Ζεύς is attested from Mycenaean di-we / Diwos and Homeric Greek.
The initial Ζ- in Attic represents the voiced affricate [zd], preserving the PIE cluster *dy- from *dyēws 'sky, god of the sky'.
The diphthong ευ is long for accentual purposes and carries the acute accent, producing the single pitch peak Zeús.
The final -ς is the nominative singular ending of the archaic stem *dyēu-s.

The place name Nikkō is famous for the Tōshō-gū shrine, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu.

atlas.name: SpəntaMainyu
steps: Spənta 'holy/bounteous' is written with schwa ə (𐬆).
The Avestan spelling matches the amesha spenta epithet in the Younger Avesta.
Mainiiu ends in the diphthongal sequence -iiu.

atlas.name: VohuManah
steps: Vohu Manah is one of the Amesha Spentas praised in the Gathas.
The final -h in Vohu and Manah represents Avestan h (𐬵).
The vowel o in Vohu is written with the Avestan letter o (𐬊).

atlas.name: AšaVahišta
steps: Aṣ̌a 'Truth' begins with the Avestan letter ṣ̌ (𐬴).
Vahišta shows the Avestan treatment of š (𐬱) and h (𐬵).
The phrase appears throughout the Gathas as the highest Asha.

atlas.name: XšaθraVairya
steps: The initial cluster xš- is written with x (𐬑) and š (𐬱).
The medial θ in Xšaθra corresponds to the Avestan letter θ (𐬚).
Vairiia writes the glide -y- with a doubled i (𐬌𐬌), a common Avestan orthography.

atlas.name: SpəntaĀrmaiti
steps: Spənta uses schwa ə (𐬆) before the n (𐬥).
Ārmaiti begins with long ā (𐬁).
The goddess is named in the Gathas as the personification of devotion.

atlas.name: Haurvatāt
steps: Haurvatāt is one of the Amesha Spentas, associated with wholeness.
The long final āt is written with ā (𐬁) plus t (𐬙).
The sequence au is written with a (𐬀) followed by u (𐬎).

atlas.name: Amərətāt
steps: Amərətāt pairs with Haurvatāt as the Amesha Spenta of immortality.
Both medial vowels are schwa ə (𐬆).
The ending -tāt uses long ā (𐬁) before final t (𐬙).

atlas.name: Sraoša
steps: Sraoša is the Avestan yazata of obedience and divine hearing.
The š sound is written with Avestan š (𐬱).
The diphthong ao is written with a (𐬀) followed by o (𐬊).

atlas.name: Rašnu
steps: Rašnu is the yazata of justice who weighs souls.
The š is written with Avestan letter š (𐬱).
The final u is the short vowel u (𐬎).

atlas.name: Anāhitā
steps: Anāhitā's full Avestan epithet is Arəduuī Sūrā Anāhitā.
The long ī in Arəduuī and long ū in Sūrā are written with distinct letters (𐬍, 𐬏).
The common name Anāhitā begins with a-, long ā-, h, i, t, ā.

atlas.name: Wꜣḏyt
steps: The Egyptian name is written 𓇅𓏏𓆗 in hieroglyphs.
Hieroglyphs combine logograms, phonograms, and determinatives; the exact function of each sign depends on context.
Egyptian writing does not record vowels; the vocalised form is a modern convention reconstructed from Coptic and Greek evidence.
The Unicode restoration Wꜣḏyt uses Egyptological alef/ayin and other registrable characters; the hieroglyphic form is not registrable in .com.

atlas.name: Búri
steps: ᛒ (bjarkan) writes /b/.
ᚢ (úr) writes /u/ and /ú/.
ᚱ (reið) writes /r/.
ᛁ (ís) writes /i/.
The runic spelling reflects normalized Old Norse Búri; Younger Futhark does not distinguish short and long vowels.
